selection: the main reason of each global problem
description: The most relevant reason of each global problem of the start page ranking with the potential loss that it causes, shown in the reason column of the ranking beside the climate gas emissions of global warming (solution_prio.json). The most relevant reason is the reason whose mechanism the annual potential loss of the problem measures, as the description of the annual GDP share in the problem file states, so this reason causes the whole loss of the row: its loss is the annual GDP share of the problem times the world GDP of 110.047 trillion EUR, the same calculation as the potential loss of the row. Each reason is the phrase of the reasons file of the problem, repeated here with the same definition. A value names the problem itself, because the start page takes it into the reason column of the problem row; it carries 'assumed', because the annual GDP share it is calculated from is assumed. This file is imported last, so that the database ids of every other phrase stay unchanged.

words.name: overrun
words.description: the amount by which the actual value exceeds the planned or estimated value

words.name: misallocation
words.description: the spending of public money on other things than the ones the citizens need and prefer

words.name: revision
words.description: the change of a published statistical number by the statistical office, e.g. after new data sources, a new base year or new methods

words.name: hunger
words.description: the chronic undernourishment: a habitual food intake that is too low to provide the dietary energy for a normal, active and healthy life

triples.name: growth loss
triples.description: the growth of the GDP per capita that is lost compared to a counterfactual without the cause

triples.name: election interference
triples.description: the attempt of a foreign or domestic actor to influence the voters of an election with false or misleading content

triples.name: cost overrun
triples.description: the actual cost above the estimated cost as share of the estimated cost

triples.name: budget misallocation
triples.description: a public budget that is spent on other purposes than the citizens would choose, e.g. less on health and sanitation

triples.name: GDP revision
triples.description: the change of the measured GDP level when the statistical office rebases the national accounts; an increase is positive
